# Results — Study 146 (Country-Momentum) on real monthly ETF tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Strategy: rotate monthly into the
top-4 single-country ETFs ranked by trailing 12-1 month total return (12 months of return,
skipping the most recent month). Universe: 23 country ETFs. Benchmarks: equal-weight all-country
basket and a random-rotation control (50 seeds). As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Tickers | N months | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|--:|---|
| Yahoo (yfinance, auto-adjust=True) | 1996-04 -> 2026-06 | 23 country ETFs | 363 | `33c0c8c86392` |

Key tickers and their earliest month-end: EWJ/EWG/EWU/EWA/EWC/EWH/EWL/EWP/EWQ/EWI/EWD/EWN/EWO/EWS/EWK/EWW/EWM start **1996-04**; EWY/EWT **2000-06**; EWZ **2000-08**; EZA **2003-03**; EIS/THD **2008-04**.

## The honest test — top-4 momentum vs equal-weight and random-rotation (gross, cost=0)

| Arm | N months | Ann. return | Ann. vol | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Momentum top-4** | 363 | **+10.2%** | 20.4% | **+0.50** | −62.3% | −0.60 | **+2.55** |
| Equal-weight basket | 363 | +9.1% | 18.6% | +0.49 | −59.1% | −0.48 | +2.54 |
| Random-rotation (50 seeds, mean) | 363 | +9.3% | — | — | — | — | — |

**Active return vs EW:** +1.1%/yr, Sharpe +0.13, HAC *t* = **+0.70** — indistinguishable from
zero. The 12-1 sort earns in absolute terms (driven by equity beta), but its **active** contribution
above merely holding all countries is economically tiny and statistically weak.

**Bootstrap 95% CI on absolute Sharpe:** [+0.10, +0.91] (only 1% of resamples negative). The
momentum portfolio is *not* distinguishable from zero in absolute terms, but the active return vs
an informed benchmark is.

## Sub-period stability — the edge has faded

The full-sample |*t*| = 2.55 hides meaningful instability:

| Period | Mom ann. | Mom Sharpe | HAC *t* | EW Sharpe | Active (mom − EW) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1996–2009** | +11.0% | +0.48 | +1.55 | +0.47 | +1.3% |
| **2010–2019** | +3.8% | +0.25 | +0.90 | +0.31 | **−0.5%** (EW wins) |
| **2020–2026** | +10.1% | +0.62 | +1.67 | +0.72 | **−0.4%** (EW wins) |

In the 2010s and 2020s, the **equal-weight basket beats or ties the momentum sort** — the
alpha has reversed sign. This is consistent with the post-publication decay documented in
Asness et al. (2013) and the general post-2010 weakness of cross-sectional momentum.

## Cost sweep — the Sharpe is fragile

At the natural monthly rebalance cadence (ETF bid-ask ~ 3-10 bps round-trip):

| Round-trip cost | Net ann. return | Net Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +10.2% | +0.50 | +2.55 |
| 5 bps | +9.9% | +0.48 | +2.47 |
| 10 bps | +9.6% | +0.47 | +2.40 |
| 20 bps | +9.0% | +0.44 | +2.24 |
| 40 bps | +7.8% | +0.38 | +1.93 |

The Sharpe is positive across the cost range because the absolute equity beta is positive — the
strategy is long equities. The *active* return vs the EW benchmark (which carries the same beta)
is already near zero gross, so any cost destroys it.

## K sensitivity (gross, 0 cost)

| K (top countries) | Ann. return | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2 | +9.8% | +0.43 | +2.24 |
| 3 | +10.7% | +0.51 | +2.58 |
| 4 | +10.2% | +0.50 | +2.55 |
| 5 | +10.1% | +0.51 | +2.57 |
| 6 | +9.5% | +0.49 | +2.44 |

All k values yield similar results, suggesting the strategy's return profile is dominated by the
equity beta of being long any subset of the country basket, not by genuine cross-sectional
momentum selection.

## Synthetic positive control

On a deterministic synthetic panel with baked-in persistent cross-country drifts
(`mom_strength=0.04, phi=0.94`), the 12-1 sort earns +45.2%/yr vs the random-rotation control
at HAC *t* = +10.51. On the null (`mom_strength=0.0`), active return vs random = +0.8%/yr,
*t* = +0.39. The machinery works; the real tape has little systematic drift to harvest.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The absolute HAC *t* is +2.55 over 30 years, but the *active* return vs
  equal-weight is only +1.1%/yr with *t* = +0.70 — not significant. The sub-periods confirm
  the edge has faded since 2010: the momentum sort *underperforms* simple equal-weighting in
  both the 2010s and 2020s. Full-sample significance is mainly equity beta, not cross-country
  momentum alpha. WEAK is generous.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The gross absolute Sharpe is positive, but the active return vs
  the trivial equal-weight benchmark is near zero before costs and negative after any realistic
  ETF transaction cost. The strategy lives or dies on the equity-beta tailwind, not a genuine
  rotation edge. An implementer needs to be long equities anyway; adding the country-sort
  rotation barely changes outcomes.
- **3rd axis — Survivorship:** The current 23-ETF list (some tickers launched after the period
  under test) projects back. Results are an upper bound; a live portfolio in 1996 would have
  fewer choices and potentially worse liquidity.
